Class RigidPhysicsApiImpl

java.lang.Object
cn.gtedd.rigidphysics.paper.api.RigidPhysicsApiImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
RigidPhysicsAPI
@Internal public final class RigidPhysicsApiImpl extends Object implements RigidPhysicsAPI
RigidPhysicsAPI 的唯一实现。

生命周期

本实例在 onEnable() 末尾创建并注册，在 onDisable() 注销， 跨 /gtrp admin reload 存活。因此下游可以长期持有它 —— 各子服务都是每次调用现取内部对象，重载换掉的是它们指向的东西，不是本实例。

三个无状态的子服务（刚体、坍塌、材质）在构造时建好复用； 视角效果服务是个例外，它跟着可选的 CameraRollService 走， 因此每次现包一层。

  • Field Details

    • API_VERSION

      public static final String API_VERSION
      API 契约版本。

      它与插件版本各自演进：实现修 bug 发 1.0.3 时这个常量不动， 因为契约没变。只有 api 模块新增/调整了公开成员才该动它，且要遵循语义化版本。 改这里时记得同步 api/build.gradle.kts 的发布版本与 README 的示例。

    • apiVersion

      @NotNull public @NotNull String apiVersion()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      The API contract version, such as "1.0.0", following semantic versioning.

      This value tracks the api module and evolves independently of the plugin implementation version: when the implementation ships 1.0.3 to fix a bug, the API version stays 1.0.0 — because the contract did not change. If your plugin has a hard requirement on some newly added capability, compare against this value rather than RigidPhysicsAPI.implementationVersion().

      Specified by:

    • isPhysicsAvailable

      public boolean isPhysicsAvailable()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Whether the physics runtime is actually available.

      Typical reasons for false: the server CPU architecture is unsupported, the native library failed to load, or the physics thread has stopped after a fatal error. The sub-services remain safe to call in that state — they simply have no effect.

      Specified by:
      isPhysicsAvailable in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      true once the native physics runtime is ready

      @NotNull public StructuralIntegrityService structure()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Load-bearing structure service: evaluate structural integrity, query weak points, and annotate region templates.

      The split against RigidPhysicsAPI.collapses() is "look" versus "do": the collapse service makes a building fall, this one tells you whether it would without changing the world (region annotation aside). Use it for structure scanners, AI target selection, and level acceptance checks.

    • settle

      @NotNull public SettleService settle()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Settle rule service: once debris comes to rest, does it become a real block, a dropped item, or nothing at all.

      The division of labour against RigidPhysicsAPI.collapses() is "process" versus "result": the collapse service brings the building down, this one decides what is left on the ground afterwards. Without it the whole physics layer is just a visual effect and the terrain comes out untouched.

      Besides queries it also allows rules to be overridden at runtime — this is meant for ephemeral worlds: an arena is recreated every round with a UUID in its name, so a server owner has no way to write it into settle.yml.

      Specified by:
      settle in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the settle rule service, never null

    • debris

      @NotNull public @NotNull ExplosionDebrisService debris()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Explosion debris service: turn blocks destroyed outright by an explosion into scattering physics debris.

      How this differs from RigidPhysicsAPI.collapses(): collapse handles the blocks that lost their support, debris handles the blocks that were blown apart — which in vanilla simply vanish. This service sends them flying instead.

    • vehicles

      @NotNull public @NotNull VehicleService vehicles()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Real physics vehicle service: spawn handles for wheeled vehicles, manual driving input, and the built-in "look to steer" player driving mode.

      Vehicles are driven by jolt-jni's VehicleConstraint — four independently suspended wheels plus engine, transmission and differential. This is fundamentally different from fake driving that nudges a rigid body with an impulse every tick.

      Specified by:
      vehicles in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the vehicle service, never null

    • mechanisms

      @NotNull public @NotNull MechanismService mechanisms()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Mechanism service: the motor control entry point for rigid bodies driven by hinge or slider constraints (windmills, revolving doors, pistons).

      Mechanisms are driven by the same constraint machinery as VehicleConstraint: a hinge (HingeConstraint) restricts a body to rotation about one axis, a slider (SliderConstraint) restricts it to translation along one axis, both with position and velocity motors.

      Specified by:
      mechanisms in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the mechanism service, never null

    • characters

      @NotNull public @NotNull CharacterService characters()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Virtual character service: characters that move through the physics world and are blocked by terrain and rigid bodies.

      Characters are driven by jolt-jni's CharacterVirtual — a kinematic capsule that does not consume rigid body budget, walks along the ground, climbs steps, and is blocked by dice and vehicles. A good foundation for NPCs that interact with the physics world.

      Specified by:
      characters in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the character service, never null

    • ragdolls

      @NotNull public @NotNull RagdollService ragdolls()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Ragdoll service: seven-part rigid body humanoid skeletons that collapse in the physics world.

      Ragdolls are driven by jolt-jni's Ragdoll — head, torso, two arms and two legs are each a dynamic rigid body, joined into a skeleton by SwingTwist constraints, falling under gravity and scatterable by a shove. A good foundation for "NPC drops dead" animations.

      Specified by:
      ragdolls in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the ragdoll service, never null

    • interaction

      @NotNull public @NotNull InteractionService interaction()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Rigid body interaction service: grab, release, throw and freeze — the foundation for physics guns and wands.

      Use it together with PhysicsBodyService.raycast(Location, Vector, double): pick the body in front of the crosshair with a ray, then grab, hover and throw it through this service. Grabbing is a stateful interaction; the state machine lives in the main plugin.

      Specified by:
      interaction in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:

    • cameraEffects

      @NotNull public @NotNull Optional<CameraEffectService> cameraEffects()
      Description copied from interface: RigidPhysicsAPI
      Camera effect service: the screen roll and shake caused by explosions and collapses.

      This returns an Optional rather than a nullable value because the feature can be switched off wholesale by the server owner (enabled: false in camera-roll.yml). When it is off the service is never constructed, so the steady-state cost is genuinely zero. That is a different situation from "physics is unavailable", and the type makes the difference explicit.

      Specified by:
      cameraEffects in interface RigidPhysicsAPI
      Returns:
      the camera effect service, or Optional.empty() when the feature is disabled
